axes.runtime:
A local Node.js child process communicating with the client over stdio.
Its lifecycle is bound to the client process — it stops when the client exits.
axes.local_files:
The core capability. **Unrestricted access is not the default**:
allowed directories must be given via command-line arguments, or delivered dynamically if the client supports the Roots protocol.
**If started with no arguments and the client does not support roots, the server errors out directly at initialization.**
axes.background:
Not supported. A local stdio process lives and dies with the client;
there is no standalone daemon or cloud-execution form.
axes.tools:
It provides 11 tools: read_text_file, read_media_file, read_multiple_files,

write_file, edit_file, create_directory, list_directory,

list_directory_with_sizes, move_file, search_files, directory_tree.
Output is structured content, ready for direct consumption.
axes.context:
Stateless. Each call is independent; no session memory is kept.
list_allowed_directories can query the currently effective directories.
axes.permissions:
**No separate approval mechanism**; the permission boundary is defined entirely by the allowed directories.
All file operations are confined to the allowed directories; anything outside is rejected.

**Note: it provides write_file / edit_file / move_file / create_directory —
a combination that is writable but has no delete tool.**
axes.fit:
Lets an Agent safely read and write text and media files inside specified directories.
Not a fit for scenarios needing delete operations or cross-directory aggregation.

mcp.transport:
stdio only. A local Node.js process communicating over standard input/output.
The official README (full-text verified 2026-10-08) gives only two local launch methods:
npx and Docker. There is no official configuration for a remote transport.
Directory control goes through command-line arguments or MCP Roots (dynamically updatable).
mcp.auth:
No separate authentication layer. In stdio form it inherits all file permissions of the client user that launches it.
The permission boundary is not an auth mechanism but a directory allowlist.
mcp.scope:
**The default scope is narrow and explicitly forced**: allowed directories must be given via command-line arguments,
or delivered dynamically if the client supports the Roots protocol.
With no arguments and no client roots support, the server errors out at initialization.

**No delete tool is provided**; write, edit, move and create-directory are.
list_allowed_directories can query the currently effective directories.

The MCP servers repo README, original wording:

> The servers in this repository are intended as **reference implementations**
> to demonstrate MCP features and SDK usage. They are meant to serve as
> educational examples for developers building their own MCP servers,
> **not as production-ready solutions**. Developers should evaluate their own
> security requirements and implement appropriate safeguards based on their
> specific threat model and use case.

> **Note**: this statement applies to every official reference server in this section;
each entry's body should keep this reminder.
sections.权限设计实测记录:
This is the most valuable design detail of this server.

| Scenario | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| Directory arguments passed at launch | The arguments become the allowed directories |
| No arguments + client supports Roots | Client roots **fully replace** server-side directories |
| No arguments + client lacks Roots | **Error at initialization** |
| Client roots change at runtime | Updated via `roots/list_changed` notification, no restart needed |

**The "no arguments + no roots support = startup failure" design deserves credit** —
it turns a potential permission escape (unrestricted file access) into an explicit failure.
sections.工具清单:
| Category | Tools |
|---|---|
| Read | `read_text_file` `read_media_file` `read_multiple_files` |
| Write | `write_file` `edit_file` |
| Directory | `create_directory` `list_directory` `list_directory_with_sizes` `move_file` `directory_tree` |
| Search | `search_files` |

**Note**: **there is no delete tool**. This is a deliberate permission-narrowing design.
